text_plugin_synopsis: Runs scripts with the embedded Auto.js 4.1.1 Alpha2 engine to compare results with AutoJs6
p_languages_all_supported: The current README.md supports the following languages
p_plugin_interface: Stable identifiers and limits for AutoJs6 host and plugin developers
p_introduction: AutoJs4 Runtime embeds the engine of [AutoJs4]({{ autojs4_url }}), the clone of {{ autojs4_baseline }} that serves as the behavioral baseline of AutoJs6. After installing it, the "Run with AutoJs4" entry in the AutoJs6 file manager runs `.js` files, `.auto` recordings and project folders with the original Rhino {{ rhino_version }} engine inside this plugin's own process, while the console output flows back into AutoJs6. This makes it possible to check on one device whether a script behaves differently on AutoJs4 and on AutoJs6 without installing AutoJs4 itself.
usage_steps: Use AutoJs6 build {{ required_host_version_code }} ({{ required_host_version_name }}) or later on Android {{ min_android_version }} (API {{ android_min_sdk }}) or later.
Install the release APK matching the device ABI (`arm64-v8a` for most current phones, `armeabi-v7a` for 32-bit devices, `x86_64` or `x86` for emulators), or the larger `universal` APK.
Open the AutoJs6 plugin center and enable AutoJs4 Runtime. If Android left the newly installed package stopped, use the host `Activate` action.

Open the plugin settings from the plugin center and grant storage access, display over other apps and the accessibility service as the scripts need them; these permissions belong to the plugin, not to AutoJs6.
In the AutoJs6 file manager, open the menu of a `.js` file, a `.auto` file or a project folder and choose `Run with AutoJs4`. The task appears in the AutoJs6 task list and can be stopped there.
p_usage_note: The plugin keeps AutoJs4 unchanged: the same Rhino {{ rhino_version }}, AutoJs4's original OpenCV {{ opencv_version }} library on armeabi-v7a and the same OpenCV release rebuilt for 64-bit devices, `targetSdk {{ android_target_sdk }}` and the same engine modules. Differences you observe between the two engines are therefore differences between AutoJs4 and AutoJs6, and can be reported to the AutoJs6 issue tracker.
p_quick_start_intro: Save this file in the AutoJs6 workspace and run it through `Run with AutoJs4`
p_quick_start_result: The AutoJs6 console prints the lines prefixed with `[AutoJs4]`; the first line shows the plugin package name that executed the script, which proves the AutoJs4 engine ran it.
compatibility_points: Engine: AutoJs4 {{ autojs4_version }} ({{ autojs4_baseline }} clone), Git commit [`{{ autojs4_commit }}`]({{ autojs4_commit_url }}), Rhino {{ rhino_version }}, OpenCV {{ opencv_version }}. The AutoJs4 sources are included as a Git submodule and compiled without modification; the arm64-v8a and x86_64 OpenCV libraries are rebuilt from the same release with NDK {{ ndk_version }} and verified to export every JNI symbol of the original library.

Platform: Android {{ min_android_version }} (API {{ android_min_sdk }}) or later. Single-ABI APKs cover `{{ supported_abis }}`; the `universal` APK contains all four. Like AutoJs4, the `x86` build has no OpenCV.

Scripts: `.js` files, `.auto` root recordings and project folders with `project.json` (the `main` script and `features` are honoured). `"ui";` scripts open AutoJs4's own script activity inside the plugin process.

Permissions: storage access (legacy external storage, `targetSdk {{ android_target_sdk }}`), display over other apps and the AutoJs4 accessibility service are granted to the plugin separately from AutoJs6. Root features use the `su` of the device like AutoJs4.

Concurrency: up to {{ max_concurrent_executions }} AutoJs4 scripts run at the same time; stopping a task in AutoJs6 stops the AutoJs4 engine, and a crashed plugin process is reported as a failed task.
security_points: The Wake activity and both exported services require `org.autojs.permission.PLUGIN`; scripts run under the plugin UID in the `:autojs4_runtime` process, never inside AutoJs6.

Scripts are addressed by absolute path. The plugin reads and writes files only with the storage permission the user granted to it, and rejects requests whose paths are not absolute or whose files cannot be read.
Console output is streamed to AutoJs6 through a bounded oneway callback in chunks of at most {{ max_log_chunk }}; the terminal event carries status, error message and stack trace summaries only.
AutoJs4's own external entry points (run intents, shortcuts, Tasker) are not exported. Only the AutoJs6 host can start scripts through the protected Binder service.
p_contract: `AutoJs4RuntimeService` is discovered by action `{{ plugin_service_action }}` and category `{{ plugin_service_category }}`. `runScript` validates the request Bundle (script path, working directory, optional project folder, arguments, delay, interval and loop count), starts the AutoJs4 execution and returns an acceptance Bundle immediately; `started`, `log` and `finished` events then arrive through the callback. `cancelScript` stops a running execution or remembers a cancellation for an execution that has not been dispatched yet. The complete contract is documented in the AutoJs6 repository ([protocol V1]({{ protocol_doc_url }})).
p_16kb_status: 16 KB page size: the arm64-v8a and x86_64 native libraries (OpenCV {{ opencv_version }} rebuilt with NDK {{ ndk_version }} and the jackpal terminal libraries rebuilt by the AutoJs6 host) are linked with a 16 KB maximum page size, and the shared alignment gate verifies every ELF PT_LOAD segment at build time. A run on a 16 KB page device has not been performed yet.
p_build_intro: Building requires JDK 17 or later, Python 3 and Android SDK 37 (the AutoJs4 engine modules compile against API 30, which the Android SDK downloads on demand). Clone with `--recurse-submodules` so that `autojs4/` is populated. The standard checks validate generated documentation, JVM tests, debug APKs, the instrumentation package and Android Lint.
p_localization: Edit the JSON and Markdown templates, then run `py .python/generate_markdown.py`. Generated README, changelog, and plugin-instruction files must not be edited by hand. The `--check` mode validates language shape, version alignment, localized resources, orphan files, and generated-file drift without writing.

p_instruction_backend: This release embeds AutoJs4 {{ autojs4_version }} (commit `{{ autojs4_commit }}`) with Rhino {{ rhino_version }} and OpenCV 3.4.3 and runs every script in the isolated `:autojs4_runtime` process. Start, console lines and completion return to AutoJs6 through the host contract; the task can be stopped from the AutoJs6 task list.
p_instruction_more: See the [project README]({{ repo_url }}) for ABI selection, permissions, the exact contract and the scope of this version.
p_icon_artwork: The launcher icon is a provisional glyph rendered by `.python/generate_provisional_icon.py` until maintainer artwork is available; verify it with `py .python/generate_provisional_icon.py --check`.
